phenotypes.label: Atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease
phenotypes.description: Atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease with hypertension and hyperlipidemia, manifesting as angina, acute myocardial infarction, and coronary artery disease. Vascular involvement extends to carotid and aortic pathology, with related findings such as hypertensive heart disease and stage 3 chronic kidney disease as common comorbidity.

phenotypes.label: Gastrointestinal disorders with bleeding/anemia
phenotypes.description: Gastrointestinal conditions dominate, spanning upper and lower tract disease with bleeding and iron deficiency anemia. Findings include GERD and gastritis with hiatal hernia; diverticulosis, hemorrhoids, rectal bleeding and melena; colonic polyps and benign neoplasms, along with inflammatory and acute abdominal conditions such as appendicitis, peritonitis, celiac disease, and inflammatory bowel disease.

phenotypes.label: Hypertension, hyperlipidemia, coronary disease
phenotypes.description: Chronic cardiometabolic comorbidity dominated by essential hypertension and dyslipidemia, with coronary atherosclerosis, valvular disease, edema, and GERD. Also includes impaired glucose tolerance/type 2 diabetes and cerebrovascular disease with post‑stroke deficits, reflecting atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease burden; more common in men and older adults.

phenotypes.label: Cardiometabolic and GI comorbidity baseline
phenotypes.description: Common chronic cardiometabolic conditions dominate, including hypercholesterolemia, hypertension, impaired fasting glycemia, atrial fibrillation, valvular disease, carotid disease, and thrombotic stroke. Gastrointestinal comorbidities such as GERD, Barrett’s esophagus, diverticular disease, and colon polyps are frequent, consistent with an older adult baseline.

phenotypes.label: Ocular disease: cataract, glaucoma, refractive errors
phenotypes.description: Cluster of ophthalmic conditions spanning dry eye, cataracts, refractive errors (presbyopia, myopia, astigmatism), and glaucomatous disease with ocular hypertension. Also includes vitreoretinal disorders (vitreous degeneration/opacities, epiretinal membrane, retinal detachment), inflammatory eye disease (iritis, scleritis), blepharitis, and age-related macular degeneration presenting with visual disturbance or impairment.

phenotypes.label: Sleep disorders with anxiety and ADHD
phenotypes.description: Prominent sleep complaints (insomnia, hypersomnia, snoring) co-occur with anxiety and stress-related disorders, fatigue, and episodic tachycardia. Attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder is frequent in this cluster, indicating a neurobehavioral–sleep symptom burden across patients.

phenotypes.label: BPH/LUTS with hearing loss
phenotypes.description: Male lower urinary tract symptoms predominate: benign prostatic hyperplasia with obstructive/irritative symptoms (nocturia, frequency, incontinence), erectile dysfunction, and raised PSA/prostate disease. Age-related auditory disorders, including sensorineural hearing loss and tinnitus, are frequent co-occurrences. This reflects predominantly male genitourinary complaints in older adults.

phenotypes.label: Acute abdominal pain and GI symptoms
phenotypes.description: Abdominal pain with prominent nausea/vomiting and diarrhea dominates, including epigastric and quadrant-localized pain with heartburn/GERD and constipation variants. Diagnoses span acute gastrointestinal syndromes such as gastroenteritis, gastritis, and appendicitis, as well as chronic inflammatory conditions including irritable bowel syndrome, Crohn’s disease, and ulcerative colitis.

phenotypes.label: Inflammatory rheumatologic and musculoskeletal disorders
phenotypes.description: Autoimmune and inflammatory rheumatology with widespread musculoskeletal pain and tendon/enthesis disorders, including rheumatoid arthritis, systemic lupus erythematosus, Sjogren's syndrome, osteoarthritis, and focal joint pains. Extra-articular features appear (episcleritis, sialadenitis, lupus anticoagulant) and connective tissue disease–associated interstitial lung disease; more common in females.

phenotypes.label: Thyroid disorders and neoplasms
phenotypes.description: Thyroid disease cluster featuring hypothyroidism (including postoperative), goiter (uni- and multinodular), autoimmune thyroiditis, and thyroid neoplasms. Associated findings include neck mass, dysphonia, hyperparathyroidism with hypocalcemia, and vitamin D deficiency. This pattern is more common in females.

phenotypes.label: Multiple sclerosis and neurologic deficits
phenotypes.description: Central nervous system symptom cluster with paresthesia, weakness, dysarthria, ataxia, and gait disturbance. Demyelinating disease is prominent (multiple sclerosis, neuromyelitis optica) with optic atrophy and white matter disease, alongside focal deficits and hemiplegia from cerebrovascular injury. Autonomic involvement with neurogenic bladder and urge incontinence, with downstream disability such as wheelchair dependence and pressure ulcers.

phenotypes.label: Allergic rhinitis, sinusitis, and asthma
phenotypes.description: Atopic upper airway disease characterized by allergic rhinitis and chronic rhinosinusitis alongside cough and asthma. Includes seasonal/pollen-driven rhinitis, nasal congestion, acute sinusitis/bronchitis episodes, and varying asthma severity. Reflects patients with allergy-driven respiratory symptoms spanning the nose, sinuses, and bronchi.

phenotypes.label: Diabetes with CKD and PVD complications
phenotypes.description: Long-standing type 2 diabetes and hypertension complicated by chronic kidney disease (including stage 3–5/end-stage), heart failure/cardiomyopathy, and coronary atherosclerosis. Prominent micro- and macrovascular sequelae include peripheral vascular disease with neuropathy, foot infection/osteomyelitis and lower‑limb amputation, as well as proliferative retinopathy and macular edema. This burden is more common in men and skews older.

phenotypes.label: Behavioral health with URIs and injuries
phenotypes.description: Blend of mood and anxiety disorders and ADHD with common upper respiratory infections (COVID-19, acute URI, otitis media, pharyngitis) and minor injuries (sprains, lacerations, burns, corneal abrasion). These are disparate outpatient problems rather than a single clinical syndrome.

phenotypes.label: Acute symptom catch-all
phenotypes.description: Nonspecific pain dominates (general, chest, shoulder, neuropathic) alongside viral and respiratory presentations such as COVID-19, fever, cough, wheeze, and sore throat. It also gathers common musculoskeletal injuries and degenerative complaints (fractures, bursitis, radiculopathy, knee pain) with baseline chronic comorbidities like hypertension, dyslipidemia, and obesity.

phenotypes.label: Female breast cancer and sequelae
phenotypes.description: Clinical pattern centers on female breast cancer, including quadrant-specific primaries, carcinoma in situ, receptor status, and abnormal mammographic findings with breast symptoms. It also includes postoperative mastectomy state, lymphedema, and regional lymph node involvement, reflecting diagnosis and local disease burden. Predominantly affects women.

phenotypes.label: HIV/AIDS with opportunistic infections
phenotypes.description: Cluster centered on HIV infection with AIDS‑defining and opportunistic infections, often with viral hepatitis co‑infection and other sexually transmitted infections. Findings include Kaposi sarcoma, esophageal candidiasis, herpes zoster complications, gonorrhea, genital herpes, anogenital warts, and recurrent cellulitis/abscesses; this pattern is more common in males.

phenotypes.label: Colorectal cancer with stoma complications
phenotypes.description: Rectal, sigmoid, and anal malignancies with ileostomy/stoma presence and complications, paralytic ileus, gastrointestinal hemorrhage with posthemorrhagic anemia, and episodes of hypotension or hypovolemic shock. Frequent post-procedural issues include surgical-site infection, abdominal wall abscess or hernia, and sepsis, with associated findings such as ascites, liver involvement, pleural effusion, atelectasis, and abnormal lung imaging. Overall, this reflects colorectal cancer with ostomy-related and postoperative gastrointestinal complications.

phenotypes.label: Type 1 diabetes with complications
phenotypes.description: Pattern of type 1 diabetes with acute metabolic derangements (hyperglycemia and hypoglycemia, acidosis, dehydration, hyperosmolality) and chronic complications including retinopathy, autonomic neuropathy with gastroparesis, proteinuria/microalbuminuria, and peripheral circulatory disease. Severe illness features such as acute kidney injury, sepsis, and acute hypoxemic respiratory failure also appear in some encounters.

phenotypes.label: Psoriatic arthritis with foot enthesopathy
phenotypes.description: Psoriatic disease with peripheral joint and enthesis involvement, centered on the feet and ankles (foot/ankle arthralgia, bilateral foot pain, plantar fascia disorders, Achilles bursitis). Psoriasis and psoriatic arthropathy co-occur with hand/shoulder pain and spine arthritis, consistent with a spondyloarthropathy spectrum.

phenotypes.label: Hematuria, bladder neoplasm, and COPD
phenotypes.description: Urologic conditions centered on hematuria, cystitis, kidney/ureteral stones with hydronephrosis, and bladder mass/neoplasm. Co-occurring pulmonary disease includes COPD/emphysema with dyspnea and abnormal lung imaging. This reflects patients with concurrent lower urinary tract pathology and chronic obstructive lung disease.

phenotypes.label: Dermatologic conditions and urinary symptoms
phenotypes.description: The leading conditions blend benign skin lesions and rashes (actinic keratoses, melanocytic nevi, verruca, xerosis, nail dystrophy) with lower urinary tract symptoms such as frequency and urgency, plus unrelated routine findings like impacted cerumen and sexual activity status. These span different organ systems without a unifying mechanism, so this is not a single coherent clinical phenotype.

phenotypes.label: Inflammatory skin and follicular disorders
phenotypes.description: Cluster of inflammatory and follicular skin diseases including acne (vulgaris and cystic), rosacea, seborrheic/atopic/contact dermatitis, hidradenitis suppurativa, keratosis pilaris, and pseudofolliculitis. It also includes benign cutaneous lesions and pigmentary conditions (melanocytic nevi, seborrheic and other keratoses, post‑inflammatory hyperpigmentation, chloasma), with occasional superficial infections and non‑scarring alopecia.

phenotypes.label: Gynecologic and menopausal disorders
phenotypes.description: Women’s gynecologic and menopausal disorders centered on uterine pathology (fibroids, endometrial hyperplasia/carcinoma), vaginitis/atrophic vaginitis, ovarian cysts, and postmenopausal bleeding. Frequently accompanied by urinary symptoms and infections with mixed urinary incontinence; markedly more common in females.

phenotypes.label: Migraine and headache disorders
phenotypes.description: Primary headache syndromes centered on migraine, including with and without aura, chronic/refractory forms, status migrainosus, and tension-type headache. Associated features include dizziness/vertigo, neck pain with cervico-occipital neuralgia, benign intracranial hypertension, and posttraumatic headache. This pattern is more common in females and skews younger.

phenotypes.label: Type 2 diabetes with complications
phenotypes.description: Type 2 diabetes with frequent poor control and classic micro- and macrovascular complications. Features include diabetic neuropathy, retinopathy, kidney disease, peripheral arterial disease and foot ulcers, alongside hypertension, hyperlipidemia, obesity, and coronary atherosclerosis; more common in men and older adults.

phenotypes.label: Sleep apnea with psychiatric comorbidity
phenotypes.description: Obstructive sleep apnea with insomnia and obesity, co-occurring with depression and post‑traumatic stress disorder. Otologic symptoms including bilateral sensorineural hearing loss and tinnitus, along with mild cognitive complaints, are common in this cluster. This pattern is more prevalent in men.

phenotypes.label: Serious mental illness with polysubstance use
phenotypes.description: Severe mental illness with polysubstance use, including nicotine dependence; alcohol, opioid, cocaine, cannabis, and stimulant use disorders; bipolar and schizophrenia‑spectrum disorders; PTSD; and suicidal ideation. Soft‑tissue infections, injuries, alcoholic gastritis, and dental disease appear alongside. More common in males and skews younger.

phenotypes.label: Epilepsy and acute intracranial disorders
phenotypes.description: Neurologic cluster centered on seizure disorders and epilepsy, including complex partial and refractory forms and status epilepticus. Co-occurring intracranial conditions include encephalitis and meningitis, brain neoplasms (including meningioma and primary malignant brain tumors), traumatic brain injury with cerebral edema or skull-base fracture, hydrocephalus, and late effects of stroke such as aphasia and cognitive deficits. Presentations often include loss of consciousness, syncope, altered mental status, dizziness, and headache.

phenotypes.label: Graves disease with ophthalmopathy
phenotypes.description: Pattern of hyperthyroidism/Graves disease with ophthalmic involvement. Prominent features include thyrotoxicosis and toxic diffuse goiter with exophthalmos and diplopia, plus palpitations and cardiac arrhythmias; patients often have abnormal thyroid function with muscle symptoms and general malaise.

phenotypes.label: Pulmonary embolism and deep vein thrombosis
phenotypes.description: Venous thromboembolism centered on pulmonary embolism and lower-extremity deep vein thrombosis, presenting with dyspnea, chest pain, hypoxemia, and abnormal breathing. Cor pulmonale and pulmonary hypertension appear, with hypercoagulable states and hereditary thrombophilia (including sickling disorders) frequently recorded.

phenotypes.label: Acute symptom presentations
phenotypes.description: Broad acute-symptom cluster spanning gastrointestinal (nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, constipation, abdominal pain), respiratory (shortness of breath, wheeze, rales), and general complaints (pain, chest pain, syncope, bleeding, itching, anxiety). This reflects common presentations in urgent and primary care rather than a single disease. It skews younger.

phenotypes.label: Plasma cell dyscrasias with end-organ damage
phenotypes.description: Pattern of plasma cell dyscrasias—multiple myeloma and monoclonal gammopathy—with classic end‑organ involvement. Features include anemia, hypercalcemia, renal disease (proteinuria, nephrotic/nephritic syndrome, acute kidney injury), and lytic bone complications such as pathological vertebral fractures. Associated conditions include amyloidosis, peripheral neuropathy, cytopenias, electrolyte disturbances, edema, arrhythmias, thrombosis, and device-related bleeding complications.

phenotypes.label: Obesity and metabolic syndrome
phenotypes.description: Obesity and morbid obesity cluster with prediabetes, hypertension, dyslipidemia, and nonalcoholic fatty liver disease, forming a metabolic syndrome profile. Obstructive sleep apnea, GERD, vitamin D deficiency, and related metabolic abnormalities commonly co-occur.

phenotypes.label: Knee osteoarthritis and lower-extremity pain
phenotypes.description: Musculoskeletal degenerative disease centered on the knee, dominated by knee osteoarthritis with bilateral knee pain, effusions, and mechanical symptoms. Related lower-extremity conditions cluster here, including hip and ankle osteoarthritis, meniscal injuries, patellar tendon disorders, bursitis, sprains, and complications around joint prostheses.

phenotypes.label: Mood and anxiety disorders
phenotypes.description: Cluster of psychiatric morbidity dominated by anxiety and depressive disorders, including generalized anxiety, panic disorder, major depressive disorder (recurrent and remitted), and dysthymia. PTSD, OCD, eating disorders, insomnia, and somatic symptom presentations (e.g., palpitations) co-occur. Within this cohort it skews younger.

phenotypes.label: Pregnancy and obstetric complications
phenotypes.description: Reproductive health and obstetric care, centered on pregnancy across trimesters with high‑risk pregnancy, breech presentation, premature rupture of membranes, preterm labor, anemia of pregnancy, and pregnancy complicated by chronic conditions. Also includes gynecologic disorders such as polycystic ovary syndrome, ovarian cysts, irregular or heavy menses, vaginitis, pelvic pain, and genitourinary bleeding. Concentrated in younger, female, reproductive‑age patients.

phenotypes.label: Movement disorders with syncope and arrhythmias
phenotypes.description: Cluster of atrial fibrillation, bradycardia/sick sinus, and syncope alongside movement disorders (essential tremor, Parkinson’s spectrum) and autonomic instability (orthostatic hypotension, dizziness). Sleep disturbance, dysphagia, gait impairment, foot deformities, and pressure-related skin injury suggest frailty; this pattern skews older and is more common in men.

phenotypes.label: Chronic spine pain with radiculopathy
phenotypes.description: Pattern of chronic back and neck pain from degenerative spine disease, with radiculopathy and spinal stenosis. Includes spondylosis, disc degeneration, sciatica and lumbago with sciatica, and related shoulder or upper-limb pain.

phenotypes.label: Osteoporosis and osteoarthritis with fractures
phenotypes.description: Age-related bone and joint disease with prominent osteoporosis and osteoarthritis, accompanied by vitamin D deficiency and generalized bone/soft-tissue disorders. Features include osteoporotic fractures, tendinopathies (rotator cuff, Achilles), venous insufficiency with edema, and polymyalgia/seronegative rheumatoid arthritis, reflecting an older, predominantly female musculoskeletal burden.

phenotypes.label: Lymphoma with chemotherapy-induced cytopenias
phenotypes.description: Patients with non-Hodgkin and B‑cell lymphomas show prominent treatment-related cytopenias (neutropenia, pancytopenia, anemia) and fever. Oral mucositis, leukopenia, thrombocytopenia, and infection signals such as varicella reflect immunosuppression and chemotherapy complications in this cancer subgroup.

phenotypes.label: Non-Hodgkin lymphoma with immunodeficiency
phenotypes.description: Cluster of B‑cell non‑Hodgkin lymphomas with prominent lymphadenopathy (head/neck and retroperitoneal nodes) and occasional extranodal involvement (salivary gland, orbit). Immune dysfunction with hypogammaglobulinemia and systemic symptoms such as fatigue and malaise are common features.

phenotypes.label: Hepatobiliary–pancreatic and neuroendocrine cancers
phenotypes.description: Cancer patients with hepatocellular and intrahepatic bile duct carcinoma, pancreatic malignancies (including head of pancreas), and neuroendocrine (carcinoid) tumors. The pattern features liver involvement with cirrhosis, portal hypertension, ascites, and secondary hepatic metastases, alongside cancer-related fatigue, anorexia, nausea, diarrhea, and drug‑induced polyneuropathy.

phenotypes.label: Cancer with lymphadenopathy and effusions
phenotypes.description: Cancer patients with prominent lymphadenopathy, dysphagia and esophageal symptoms, alongside thoracic complications such as pleural and pericardial effusions, hemoptysis, chest pain, and dyspnea. Lifted conditions point to head and neck and breast malignancies with oral mucosal involvement, multiple lung nodules, and hepatosplenomegaly, consistent with locoregional and metastatic disease burden; this pattern skews slightly younger within the cohort.

phenotypes.label: Prostate cancer and urinary complications
phenotypes.description: Prostate cancer with coexisting prostate disorders (BPH, prostatitis) and PSA elevation. Characterized by lower urinary tract symptoms and complications—urinary obstruction/retention, nocturia, incontinence, and erectile dysfunction—and concentrated in older men.

phenotypes.label: Ovarian/testicular cancers with metastases
phenotypes.description: Pattern of ovarian and testicular primary malignancies with spread to peritoneum/retroperitoneum and intra‑abdominal lymph nodes, often with pulmonary nodules and lung metastases. Associated findings include intra‑abdominal or pelvic masses, localized lymphadenopathy, and obstructive uropathy such as hydronephrosis, with nonspecific symptoms like nausea and constipation.

phenotypes.label: Skin cancer and precursor lesions
phenotypes.description: Cutaneous malignancies are prominent, including squamous cell carcinoma, basal cell carcinoma, and melanoma, accompanied by actinic damage and precursor lesions (actinic keratoses, solar lentigines) and dysplastic nevi. Patients often have multiple nevi and pigmentary skin changes documented on exam.

phenotypes.label: Lung cancer with ocular disease
phenotypes.description: Pattern centers on lower respiratory tract malignancy, with some patients coded for anatomic absence of a lung. There is prominent age-related ocular disease (cataract, age-related macular degeneration, retinal vascular occlusions, vitreous degeneration, refractive errors) alongside nonmelanoma skin cancers of sun‑exposed facial sites (basal and squamous cell). Within the cancer subgroup, this cluster skews older.

phenotypes.label: Head and neck cancer complications
phenotypes.description: Upper aerodigestive tract cancers centered on head and neck and esophagus, often with regional lymph node involvement. Prominent dysphagia with mucositis/ulcerative stomatitis, xerostomia, taste changes, neck mass, and lymphedema; many have gastrostomy or tracheostomy present with occasional device complications. Within this cancer cohort it skews toward older men.

phenotypes.label: Cardiovascular disease in cancer patients
phenotypes.description: Cancer patients with a heavy cardiovascular burden, centered on ischemic heart disease, prior myocardial infarction, congestive heart failure, cardiomyopathy, and cardiomegaly. Valvular disease (aortic, mitral, tricuspid), atrial fibrillation and other ventricular/sinus arrhythmias, and structural changes (right atrial enlargement, LVH) are prominent, with associated thoracic findings such as chest pain, pneumothorax, atelectasis, and pleural thickening.

phenotypes.label: Leukemias with transplant complications
phenotypes.description: Hematologic cancers centered on acute and chronic leukemias and related marrow disorders (e.g., AML, ALL, CML, myelodysplastic syndrome) with prominent cytopenias and leukocytosis. Many patients have history of bone marrow transplant with post‑transplant complications such as graft‑versus‑host disease and disorders affecting transplanted structures, alongside associated abnormalities like electrolyte disturbances, edema, and diarrhea.

phenotypes.label: Cutaneous melanoma with nodal disease
phenotypes.description: Cutaneous melanoma dominates, spanning head/neck, trunk, and limb sites, alongside other primary skin cancers. Lymph‑node involvement and secondary skin malignancy codes suggest regional spread, with mass or lump presentations; this pattern skews older within the cancer cohort.

phenotypes.label: Kidney/urinary cancer with CKD
phenotypes.description: Kidney and urinary tract malignancies with substantial chronic kidney disease burden. Findings include renal masses, CKD (including hypertensive CKD) with episodes of acute kidney failure and hyperkalemia, and sequelae such as absent or transplanted kidney. Within this subgroup it is more common in men and skews older.

phenotypes.label: Cervical cancer with pelvic/anorectal sequelae
phenotypes.description: Gynecologic malignancy centered on cervical cancer and cervical dysplasia with pelvic pain, dyspareunia, vaginal dryness, urinary tract infections, and anemia. Anorectal and colorectal conditions co-occur (hemorrhoids, rectal cancer, radiation proctitis, tubular adenomas) with myelosuppression and acute postoperative pain, reflecting pelvic cancer with local complications and treatment-related effects.

phenotypes.label: Lymphoma with infectious complications
phenotypes.description: Clinical pattern of Hodgkin and non-Hodgkin lymphoma with lymphadenopathy, anemia, coagulation abnormalities, and cytopenias (drug‑induced neutropenia, thrombocytopenia). Patients often present with neutropenic fever, abnormal temperature, and infectious complications including bacterial pneumonia and systemic inflammatory response. Some records note second primary malignancy, transplant status, and imaging abnormalities in thoracic or intra‑abdominal lymph nodes.

phenotypes.label: Lung cancer with respiratory complications
phenotypes.description: Primary lung malignancy with prominent respiratory symptom burden and complications, including dyspnea, cough, pleural effusion, atelectasis, and pneumothorax. COPD/emphysema, abnormal chest imaging, and reduced pulmonary function commonly accompany this pattern. The phenotype skews older.

phenotypes.label: Myeloproliferative neoplasms (ET, PV)
phenotypes.description: BCR-ABL–negative myeloproliferative neoplasms centered on essential thrombocythemia and polycythemia vera, with erythrocytosis and thrombocytosis. A subset shows iron overload/hemochromatosis with hepatocellular carcinoma and hypogonadism; within the cancer cohort this pattern skews male and older.

phenotypes.label: Cutaneous carcinoma and actinic damage
phenotypes.description: Cutaneous malignancy phenotype centered on basal and squamous cell carcinomas across face, trunk, and extremities with prominent actinic keratoses and other photodamage changes. Premalignant and uncertain-behavior skin lesions, nevi, hyperkeratosis, and phototoxic dermatitis cluster together. Within the cancer cohort, this pattern skews older and is more common in men.

phenotypes.label: Neuroendocrine and adrenal-pituitary neoplasms
phenotypes.description: Patients with neuroendocrine and adrenal–pituitary malignancies, often featuring carcinoid syndrome, adrenal tumors, pituitary adenomas, and hypopituitarism. Gastrointestinal involvement is common (colon malignancy, GERD, diverticular disease), with accompanying mood and cardiopulmonary comorbidity. Within the cancer cohort, this phenotype skews older.

phenotypes.label: Metastatic solid cancers with bone/brain
phenotypes.description: Advanced solid malignancies with frequent lung, soft‑tissue, and oral cavity primaries, complicated by metastases to bone, brain, pleura, and intrathoracic lymph nodes. Associated findings include malignant ascites, cancer‑related pain, anemia, nutritional deficiency, constipation, enlarged nodes, and postoperative/radiation‑related conditions.
